meta.title: Conflict Watchlist
meta.notes: Fully automated register: a scheduled open-source review rewrites this file daily (procedure in docs/WATCHLIST-REVIEW.md) and an hourly GitHub Action refreshes the live reporting feed (watchlist-live.json) from GDELT. Every comparison the dashboard shows (state moves, changed dimensions, the attention-score bonuses) is made against the register as it stood compareDays (7) days ago, taken from each item's `snapshots` (one entry per review: date, state and the five dimensions). Each review: (1) set reviewDate/previousReviewDate, (2) for every item set the new `now` on the five dimensions and the new `state`, then append today's snapshot (keep the last 60), (3) rewrite `status` (`summary`: plain-language current status whose first sentence states the newest development; `sources`: 2–3 links to the newest reporting), `whyNow`, `topic` and `whyMatters` (stable framing, revise only on a phase change), `changes` (dated bullets covering the last 7 days: keep those still inside the window, add today's, drop older ones), `next`, `ignore` and `sources`, (4) record any state move in `history` and keep `timeline` (4–8 dated one-line events of the current phase, chronological) current. The dashboard derives attention rank, movements, changed-dimension flags, staleness, coverage surges — do not type those in. `next` holds named, checkable indicators.

phase.label: Conflict phase
phase.desc: A short label for the stage the conflict is in (for example attritional war, ceasefire without implementation, grey-zone contest). It sits under the current-status summary and shows the label from 7 days ago when it changed.

escalation.label: Escalation risk
escalation.desc: How likely a step up in intensity or a change of phase is in the coming weeks.

levels.Low: Stable; no live trigger and restraints hold.
levels.Moderate: Triggers exist (deadlines, disputes, incidents) but restraints are holding.
levels.High: Active exchanges or a named trigger that is likely to fire; a phase change is plausible within weeks.
levels.Severe: Active war or ongoing kinetic exchange with strategic stakes (major shipping lanes, energy, great-power forces).

tempo.label: Operational tempo
tempo.desc: How much military activity is actually happening in the review window.

levels.Medium: Recurring incidents or steady, limited operations (patrols, fortification, occasional strikes).
levels.High: Daily strikes or operations across fronts.

adaptation.label: Adaptation behaviour
adaptation.desc: How much new tactical or technical behaviour appeared in the window; this is where the Army learning sits.

levels.Low: Both sides are using the same methods as before.
levels.High: Novel, repeatable adaptations appeared (new weapons employment, counter-measures, doctrine shifts).

sgExposure.label: Singapore exposure
sgExposure.desc: How directly the conflict touches Singapore's interests. Not shown as a register column; it still feeds the attention score and the expanded row.

levels.Moderate: An ASEAN or diplomatic role, observer contributions, or supply-chain spillover.
levels.High: Direct effect on sea lanes, energy or shipping, a Singapore-flagged vessel affected, or relevance to deployments.

attentionScore.desc: Deterministic, explainable rank. state (Priority 40 / Active 25 / Watch 10 / Archive 0) + escalation risk (Severe 20 / High 15 / Moderate 8 / Low 2) + 5 per dimension that changed over the last 7 days (compareDays) + 10 if the state moved up over the same window + Singapore exposure (High 8 / Moderate 4 / Low 0) + tier (T1 6 / T2 3 / T3 0) + 8 if the live open-source feed shows a coverage surge (see definitions.feed.surgeRule). Items flagged ignore-for-now are shown but ranked last.

feed.source: GDELT DOC 2.0 API (open, no key). Per item: 30-day daily article counts (TimelineVolRaw) and the most relevant English-language articles of the last 7 days (ArtList, HybridRel). Synced by .github/workflows/sync-watchlist-feed.yml into watchlist-live.json.
feed.surgeRule: A coverage surge is flagged when the last 7 days carry at least twice the article volume of the 7 days before and at least 20 articles; a surge adds 8 points to the attention score.
feed.titleFilter: Articles are kept only when the title contains one of the item's terms, to cut GDELT's full-text noise.
feed.terms: Title filter: at least one of these substrings must appear in an article title for it to count as reporting on the item.
feed.require: Optional groups of substrings; a title must contain at least one term from every group (two-party theatres: one term per side).
feed.exclude: Optional substrings that drop a title (sport, entertainment and other noise), in addition to the sync's global list.
feed.spamDomainsNote: Article sources dropped outright (livestream/score spam). The daily review adds domains seen producing noise.

columns.tier: Standing relevance to the Army: T1 Priority Conflicts, T2 Active Regional & Escalation Watches, T3 Baseline Regional Research Reserve. Tiers do not change week to week.
columns.state: Today's monitoring state: Priority (direct strategic relevance or high Army learning value), Active (material trend, escalation or regional relevance), Watch (baseline monitoring), Archive (reserve; revisit on a named trigger). ▲▼ marks a move over the last 7 days.
columns.status: Current status: the newest title-matched headline from the live open-source feed (synced hourly) on top, then a plain-language summary of what is happening now whose first sentence states the newest development, with links to the newest reporting it rests on. The phase label sits beneath; a struck-through label is the phase 7 days ago.
columns.coverage: Open-source coverage from the live feed (GDELT with Google News fallback): the sparkline is the last 30 days (or four weekly counts), the number is articles in the last 7 days with the change against the 7 before. 'Surge' = at least twice the prior week and at least 20 articles. Refreshes hourly.
columns.nextIndicator: The soonest dated indicator to watch, tagged with the numbered topic and watch area it informs (or 'cross-cutting' when it bears on the theatre as a whole). Expand the row for the full list.
columns.confidence: How well-sourced the assessment is: High (multiple independent, dated sources), Medium (some single-source or snippet-only items), Low (thin or contested reporting).
columns.attention: Attention score, the register's sort order. Hover a score for its breakdown.
columns.topic: Topics of interest: the three capability contests the Army follows this theatre for, set by the team (from the watchlist workbook). Numbered so they line up with the 'Why it matters' and 'Watch areas' columns; the chip is the topic's adaptability rating.
columns.whyMatters: Why it matters here: for each numbered topic, what the theatre tests (the capability, behaviour or mechanism under study).
columns.watchAreas: Watch areas: for each numbered topic, its watch status and what to monitor. Status tags: Rising (activity increasing), Established (steady pattern), Contested (the outcome is still open), Watch for trigger (review only on a named event), Background monitor, Declining.
columns.adaptability: Adaptability: how transferable the topic's lessons are to the Army — High, Medium or Low, set by the team.

watches.desc: Watches follow one thread of an item on its own once a trigger event makes it worth it: an information-operations watch (kind "info-ops": official messaging, state-media narratives and documented influence campaigns), a shadow-war watch (kind "shadow-war": sabotage, incursions, cyber and influence below the threshold of war, and the targeted side's responses) or an operation watch (kind "operation": one named military operation, its gains, the enemy's response and what it shows). Each carries a narrower daily feed, plus dated findings and an assessment researched from open sources at each review.

types.official statement: Government, foreign-ministry, military or party statement aimed at an audience (strategic communications).
types.state-media narrative: Framing pushed by state or party media, including English-language outlets aimed abroad.
types.covert information operation: Documented coordinated inauthentic behaviour, disinformation or cognitive-warfare activity, attributed by a credible reporter.
types.coercive signalling: Military, coast-guard or legal action whose purpose is the message it sends.
types.sanctions/lawfare: Sanctions, lists or legal framing used to pressure or delegitimise.
types.counter-messaging: The targeted side's official response or rebuttal.
types.domestic narrative: Narratives inside the targeted polity (parties, polls, viral claims).
types.debunked claim: A specific false claim identified by a fact-checker.
types.third-party assessment: Analysis by a think-tank, researcher or major outlet.
types.hybrid attack: Physical sabotage, arson, cable or pipeline damage, cyber attacks, GPS jamming, drone or airspace incursions and other deniable attacks below the threshold of war.
types.defensive response: The targeted side's practical countermeasures: arrests, expulsions, airspace closures, deployments, new laws and alliance consultations.
types.territorial change: Ground or settlements gained or lost, with who reports it and whether it is independently confirmed (geolocated footage, ISW).
types.official claim: A command's or ministry's claim of gains, enemy losses or prisoners that has not been independently confirmed.
types.counterattack: The opposing side's counterattacks, reinforcements or renewed assaults in the operation's sector.
types.tactic or capability: A tactic, weapon or enabler used in the operation (drones, electronic warfare, converted vehicles, shaping strikes).

items.whyNow: The first agreed local ceasefire of the year (Oleshky, from 27 Oct) and mooted mid-November talks sit alongside some of the deadliest strikes of the autumn, including a jet-drone hit on a Dnipro rail platform that killed 14 on 29 Oct. The restoration of Starlink and Starshield on 24 Oct, followed by a rise in jet-drone interception rates, is the clearest live test this week of how much layered counter-UAS depends on a third-party enabler.
changes: 29 Oct: A Russian jet-powered drone hit a train platform in Dnipro and killed at least 14, Banderol missiles killed two teenagers in Chernihiv, and drones killed three in Kremenchuk; Ukraine's Navy claimed two Su-34s destroyed by Neptune missiles at Marinovka airfield (unverified, single source); Ushakov said talks in Abu Dhabi 'after 4 Nov' would depend on the battlefield (Kyiv Independent).

28 Oct: Moscow's mayor claimed 613 Ukrainian drones were launched at the capital overnight into 29 Oct, grounding flights at Vnukovo and Domodedovo, after Ukrainian strikes hit the Novolipetsk steel plant and NAK Azot in Novomoskovsk; suspected Russian naval drones hit the container ship Constship Jet off Bulgaria (ISW, Kyiv Independent).

27 Oct: A limited Oleshky ceasefire brokered with Melania Trump took effect at 03:00 Kyiv time, running to 1 Nov with no violations reported, as Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles and 280 drones, including a double-tap strike on a university campus and a strike on the Southern Bridge; Putin told Stubb and Store that NATO 'root causes' must be resolved first (Al Jazeera, ISW).

26 Oct: Ukraine struck the Voronezh aircraft plant and a synthetic rubber plant, and Yandex said it had relocated three supercomputers after Ukrainian strikes on at least three of its data centres, as Kommersant reported plans to site critical data centres underground (ISW).

25 Oct: Russia launched 153 drones, 92 of them jet-powered, killing four in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, while Ukraine hit the Energiya plant in Yelets (Iskander power cells) and a titanium plant in Berezniki; ISW assessed that Operation Vivaldi had operationally defeated Russia's Fortress Belt plan (ISW).

24 Oct: Ukrainian officials confirmed that unrestricted Starlink and Starshield access had resumed, as Ukraine struck a chemical plant in Omsk about 2,500 km from the border and ISW reported two new Geran-5 variants with a claimed 900 km/h top speed (ISW, Kyiv Independent).

next.text: Whether the Oleshky ceasefire holds to its 22:59 1 Nov expiry, the humanitarian convoy enters and residents can choose to leave for Ukrainian-held territory (the Anapa–Gomel route is due on 31 Oct), and whether the truce is extended to other occupied areas as Lubinets suggested.
next.ifSeen: Truce extended or replicated elsewhere → phase check and flag today; violations or forced removal to Russia → note for the monthly pattern set.

next.text: Whether US–Ukraine–Russia trilateral talks convene in Abu Dhabi in mid-November ('after 4 Nov' per Ushakov on 28 Oct) with an energy and maritime ceasefire on the agenda, or are deferred against the battlefield situation.
next.ifSeen: Talks convene with an energy or maritime truce agreed → phase check and flag today; postponed → track only.

next.text: Starlink and Starshield access stays unrestricted after its 24 Oct restoration, and Ukraine's jet-drone interception rate (over 75% for 17–28 Oct per Air Force data) holds against faster Geran-5 variants.
next.ifSeen: New speed caps or interception falling back below 60% → escalate; sustained rates above 75% → note for the monthly pattern set.

next.text: Patriot interceptor deliveries above 12 a month, versus further ballistic salvos on Kyiv (more than 100 since 14 Oct per Zelensky) causing mass casualties or bridge closures.
next.ifSeen: Larger deliveries confirmed → note for the monthly pattern set; a large salvo largely unintercepted → escalate.

next.text: Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian refineries (none reported since 18 Oct under US pressure) and Russian regions reimpose fuel sales limits, or Russian strikes again leave 500,000+ Ukrainian households without power.
next.ifSeen: Either side's energy strikes resume at scale → escalate; repair and relocation throughput (e.g. data centres moved underground) → note for the monthly pattern set.

next.text: ISW or geolocated confirmation of Ukrainian advances beyond the Zherebets River north of Lyman, versus Russian gains around Kostiantynivka (Klynove, Bezimyane, Popsane, 28 Oct) threatening Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka or consolidation in Dobropillia.
next.ifSeen: Confirmed Ukrainian gains → phase check; Russian breakthrough toward Druzhkivka or Dobropillia consolidated → escalate.

timeline.text: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps revealed Operation Vivaldi, a counteroffensive near Lyman it said cleared 75 square kilometres of Russian infiltrators and liberated Serednie and nearby villages.

A daylight Russian jet-drone raid hit Kyiv's National Academy of Sciences and killed five people across Ukraine, Zelensky said Russia had begun additional mobilisation as Putin enlarged the armed forces by 15,500, and the 3rd Army Corps closed Vivaldi's third stage with 51 square kilometres, three settlements and over 250 prisoners taken using converted BTR-60s as kamikaze vehicles.
Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire that neither Kyiv nor Moscow had confirmed, and Russian forces struck the Kharkiv thermal power plant hours later.

Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and over 120 drones at energy sites around Kyiv and Kharkiv, leaving 600,000 without power, as the 3rd Army Corps claimed a fourth Vivaldi stage of 101 square kilometres north of Lyman.

Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia, setting fires at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and Ruchi depot and hitting a VK data centre about 850 km from the border, its deepest mass raid of the war.

Hours after Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg, Russia hit Kyiv with three cluster-warhead ballistic missiles, one landing between the Pechersk Lavra and a monastery, killing at least four and wounding 34.

A limited humanitarian ceasefire around occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast took effect for aid deliveries and evacuations, the first agreed local truce of the year, while Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and 280 drones.
A Russian jet-powered drone struck a passenger train platform in Dnipro and killed at least 14 people, hours after Moscow's mayor said 613 Ukrainian drones had been launched at the capital overnight.

text: On persistent ISR versus signature management and deception, the Established and Contested status holds. ISW assessed on 25, 27 and 28 Oct that Operation Vivaldi had operationally defeated Russia's Fortress Belt plan, and on 26 Oct that Russia was moving drone operators into the Lyman sector after losing Rubikon crews, yet Russian infiltration still took Bezimyane and Popsane near Kostiantynivka on 28 Oct, so small-group movement under persistent observation continues to buy ground. On EW versus alternative UAS control and layered counter-UAS, the Rising status is borne out, and the binding variable is enabler access rather than jamming: after Starlink and Starshield were restored on 24 Oct, Air Force data cited by ISW put jet-drone interception above 75% for 17–28 Oct, while Russia answered with faster Geran-5 variants and the jet drone that killed 14 at Dnipro station on 29 Oct.

On contested sustainment versus dispersed support and repair, the Established and Contested status hardens on the Russian side: Yandex relocated supercomputers on 26 Oct after Ukrainian strikes, with critical data centres to go underground, as Ukrainian drones reached Omsk on 24 Oct. Easing Russian fuel shortages since refinery strikes slowed (29 Oct) show how fast throughput recovers once pressure lapses.

status.summary: The week's most significant developments were the first agreed local truce of the year, a humanitarian ceasefire around occupied Oleshky that took effect on 27 Oct and held through 29 Oct, and continued heavy Russian strikes, including ballistic missiles and 280 drones on Kyiv on 27 Oct and a jet-drone hit on a Dnipro rail platform that killed at least 14 on 29 Oct, as Ukraine struck Omsk on 24 Oct and Moscow's mayor reported 613 drones at the capital overnight into 29 Oct. watches.trigger: Russian helicopter and drone incursions into Poland, Romania and Moldova, 23–24 Sep 2026
watches.question: Is Russia escalating a shadow war against Europe below the threshold of open war (sabotage and arson, cyber attacks, undersea cable and pipeline damage, GPS jamming, drone and airspace incursions, shadow-fleet activity, espionage, assassination plots and influence or disinformation operations), through which channels and against whom, and how are European governments and NATO responding?

findings.actor: Unidentified sea-drone operators (Ambrey: likely Russian Murena-300S-derived USVs)
findings.tactic: Sea-drone strike on merchant ship in EEZ
findings.text: Around midday on 28 Oct 2026 three uncrewed surface vessels hit the Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet about 17-21 nautical miles off Cape Kaliakra inside Bulgaria's EEZ, bound for Constanta; all 18 crew were rescued to Varna but the ship sank. A French patrol aircraft warned of a possible drone attack, yet Bulgaria could not stop it; Ambrey assessed the USV as likely derived from Russia's Murena-300S, Moscow denied involvement and no state has formally attributed it.

findings.actor: Bulgarian, Romanian and Turkish defence ministers
findings.tactic: Trilateral Black Sea early-warning and intelligence sharing
findings.text: Meeting in Sofia on 28 Oct 2026 while the Contship Jet was being hit, the three littoral states agreed to expand intelligence sharing, maritime domain awareness and early warning, and Turkey said it would keep applying the Montreux Convention as is. No escorts, patrols or interception rules were announced and the joint statement named no perpetrator, so the measure is untested; it follows a 20 Oct NATO surveillance surge that did not prevent the 23 and 28 Oct sinkings.

findings.actor: Munich General Prosecutor's Office and Bavarian police
findings.tactic: Pre-emptive arrest of paid arson cell
findings.text: Munich prosecutors announced on 28 Oct 2026 that two Belarusian men, aged 39 and 50, had been in custody since early October on suspicion of preparing arson against railway and power-transmission infrastructure in the Nuremberg area for payment by a foreign state; Der Spiegel and Romanian intelligence link them to a Russia-coordinated network. The plot was stopped before any attack, the first interdiction of this network that came ahead of the act rather than after it; German prosecutors themselves have not named Russia.

findings.actor: Russia-coordinated sabotage network (per Romania's SRI); Polish CBŚP
findings.tactic: Proxy arson at Romanian defence-industry site
findings.text: Polish police reported on 28 Oct 2026 the arrest in Warsaw of Artem S., a 25-year-old Ukrainian wanted by Romania, suspected of choosing the target and financing the 14 Sep arson at the Carfil site in Brasov next to a state arms maker; Romania's SRI says the network of post-Soviet nationals living in the EU took orders from Russia to hit arms plants. The arson itself went ahead, but within six weeks the network's organiser and two other members were in custody in Poland and Germany, so this cell has been rolled up; Moscow called the accusations baseless.

findings.actor: Cyber Army of Russia Reborn (GRU-linked, per US) and Z-Pentest
findings.tactic: Hijacking poorly secured industrial control systems
findings.text: A Bloomberg investigation relayed by Meduza on 28 Oct 2026 documented Russia-linked hacktivists causing physical effects through weakly protected industrial controls, from a Danish village pumping station (December 2024, 450 homes cut off, pipes burst; password reportedly "1234") to a Catalan transformer-factory fire, stopped winery systems and a US meatpacking ammonia leak. The method is crude but works where operators skip basic security; the response so far is sanctions, rewards and a handful of prosecutions rather than prevention, and CISA warns the groups also exaggerate their results.

findings.actor: Unidentified drone (Romanian President Dan: Russia)
findings.tactic: Aerial drone strike sinking ship off Constanta
findings.text: On the morning of 23 Oct 2026 a drone set the Comoros-flagged Khoryv on fire about 13 nautical miles off Constanta, just outside Romanian territorial waters; the ship capsized, one of 13 crew died and three were missing. Nothing was intercepted three days after NATO's Black Sea surveillance surge; President Nicusor Dan and Ursula von der Leyen blamed Russia, and Romania says it is still awaiting additional protective measures.

findings.actor: Unidentified drone (ISW: likely Russian); Moldovan police
findings.tactic: Drone overflight crashing near homes
findings.text: ISW's 23 Oct 2026 assessment relayed a Moldovan police report that drone debris fell about 100 m from a residential building near Chistelnita, Telenesti district, deep inside Moldova, and judged it a likely Russian violation of Moldovan sovereignty. The drone was not intercepted; Moldova can detect but still cannot shoot down such incursions, so the overflight pattern continues unopposed.

findings.actor: German Federal Prosecutor's Office (GBA)
findings.tactic: Arresting a defence-industry spy recruit
findings.text: On 22 Oct 2026 German federal prosecutors had a Ukrainian national, Vadym Y., arrested in Brandenburg on suspicion of gathering information for a Russian intelligence service on armoured-vehicle, ammunition and explosives production and on sites securing NATO's eastern flank, partly by approaching defence-industry staff. The arrest worked as an interdiction, but prosecutors allege he had been in contact with Russian intelligence through an intermediary since at least July 2025, so the collection ran for about 15 months before it was stopped.

findings.actor: Bundeswehr Operational Command
findings.tactic: Raising sabotage threat level, hardening bases
findings.text: Defense News reported on 21 Oct 2026 that the Bundeswehr had raised its Russian sabotage threat assessment to the second-highest level, triggered by a crashed drone found with a can of explosives near Wunstorf air base and by suspicious drone overflights of Arrow 3 and Patriot sites. The assessment says vulnerable sites can no longer be confined geographically and that drone use has crossed a red line toward lethal effects; protective measures are being strengthened at installations, but none has yet been tested against an attack.

findings.actor: Russian fishing trawlers (per a Telegraph data investigation)
findings.tactic: Trawlers loitering over undersea cables
findings.text: A Telegraph analysis of 4.5 years of Global Fishing Watch data, published on 21 Oct 2026 and relayed by UNITED24 on 22 Oct, found 17 Russian trawlers making more than 500 slow, suspicious movements over North Atlantic cables, including 337 hours over Atlantic Crossing 1 north of Scotland. An unnamed NATO official said some ships may not be fishing at all; the data do not prove espionage or any damage, and the reporting names no countermeasure (single source).

findings.actor: North Atlantic Council
findings.tactic: Surveillance surge after Black Sea ship strikes
findings.text: After the North Atlantic Council met on 20 Oct 2026, NATO said allies had sent or would send additional maritime patrol aircraft, radars, explosive-exploitation teams, intelligence personnel and drones to the Black Sea following the drone strikes on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria. The priority is better situational awareness rather than interception, and NATO still did not name a perpetrator, so whether the deployment deters further strikes is untested.

findings.actor: Unidentified arsonists (Lithuanian PM: commissioned by Russia); Lithuanian authorities
findings.tactic: Arson on Starlink sites serving Ukraine
findings.text: At about 02:00 on 18 Oct 2026 attackers tried to burn satellite antennas and a control unit at a Lithuanian firm providing connectivity for Starlink antennas used by Ukraine; incendiary liquids in 3-10 litre containers were found. The attempt failed because authorities had warned the company and security had been stepped up, a rare case of pre-emptive warning stopping the arson pattern seen in Poland and Bulgaria. PM Sinkevičius blamed Russia without presenting proof, and a pre-trial investigation is open.

assessment.text: Between 18 and 29 Oct 2026 Russia's cheapest deniable tools at sea kept working while its land-based proxy networks were increasingly rolled up. Drones sank the Khoryv off Constanta on 23 Oct, killing one sailor, and three sea drones sank the Contship Jet in Bulgaria's EEZ on 28 Oct even though a French patrol aircraft gave warning, so NATO's 20 Oct surveillance surge has improved detection but not interception. Moldova still records but cannot stop overflights, as debris near Chistelnita on 23 Oct showed. On land, defenders are getting ahead: a forewarned Lithuanian firm defeated arson on 18 Oct, Germany held two Belarusians from early October before they could burn Bavarian rail and power lines, and Poland arrested the alleged organiser of the 14 Sep Brasov arms-site fire on 28 Oct, dismantling that cell. Russia's adaptation is to shift risk offshore and into crude industrial hacking, which still causes physical damage where controls are unsecured (Bloomberg, 28 Oct).

findings.actor: Russian forces north of Lyman
findings.tactic: Infiltration raid near Zelena Dolyna
findings.text: ISW's 28 Oct 2026 assessment reported that Russian forces had recently conducted an infiltration mission north of Lyman and that geolocated footage published on 28 Oct showed Ukrainian forces striking a Russian serviceman east of Zelena Dolyna afterwards. ISW recorded no Russian advance, so infiltration into ground Vivaldi retook in its fourth phase is being detected and killed rather than gaining ground.

findings.actor: Ukrainian forces along the Zherebets (per open-source mappers)
findings.tactic: Crossing the Zherebets onto the east bank
findings.text: Euromaidan Press reported on 28 Oct 2026 that AMK Mapping and Suriyak claimed on 26 Oct that Ukrainian troops had crossed the Zherebets at several points, Suriyak naming Makiivka, Novosadove and Terny as a bridgehead, while AMK said many assaults had been repelled with rising casualties. The crossings are unconfirmed (Clément Molin could not confirm any on 20 Oct, Suriyak's own map shows west-bank positions) and ISW has reported none, so the push beyond the river is a claim, not a confirmed gain (single source).

findings.actor: Russian 25th Combined Arms Army and Western Grouping elements
findings.tactic: Ground assaults northeast and southeast of Lyman
findings.text: ISW reported Russian offensive operations in the Lyman direction on 22-23 Oct and northeast and southeast of Lyman on 24-25 and 25-26 Oct 2026, without any advance; a milblogger's 23 Oct claim of an offensive from Yampil toward Ozerne and Dibrova was not confirmed. ISW says Moscow has not formally abandoned its Fortress Belt plan despite what it calls the plan's operational defeat by Vivaldi.

findings.actor: Russian 50th Varyag Unmanned Systems Brigade
findings.tactic: Drone units replacing withdrawn Rubikon operators
findings.text: ISW assessed on 26 Oct 2026 that Russia had redeployed additional unmanned-systems elements to stabilise the Lyman front, citing the Varyag brigade's 26 Oct claim that its FPV crews were striking Ukrainian forces there, after elite Rubikon operators were reportedly withdrawn following heavy losses. This corroborates Militarnyi's 22 Oct single-video report: Russia is substituting drone formations for failed infantry pressure, but no regained ground has resulted yet.

findings.actor: NC13 unit, 3rd Assault Brigade (3rd Army Corps)
findings.tactic: UGVs and FPVs ambushing pipe infiltration
findings.text: Censor.net reported on 26 Oct 2026 that NC13 soldiers used ground robots and FPV drones to stop a Russian assault group trying to approach through a pipe during Operation Vivaldi, saying the attackers emerged in large numbers and were hit at once. The result rests on the unit's own video and account and is not independently confirmed (single source).

findings.actor: 3rd Army Corps assault infantry
findings.tactic: Small-team blockade raids behind lines
findings.text: A Kyiv Independent field report of 22 Oct 2026 described pairs and small groups infiltrating up to 5 km behind Russian lines to cut supply routes and block retreats, varying routes and timings, and encircling Shandryholove along treelines instead of storming it. A battalion commander reported minimal casualties, though 30-40% of teams were spotted by drones; the outcome rests on the units' accounts, consistent with the corps' declared 277 km² and 16 settlements by 14 Oct.

findings.actor: Russian forces in the Lyman sector
findings.tactic: Anti-personnel mines and FPV saturation
findings.text: The same 22 Oct 2026 Kyiv Independent report said anti-personnel mines caused about 80% of one unit's casualties, turned back two groups at a river crossing and hit evacuation teams, while a six-man assault faced about 35 fibre-optic FPVs and 12 Molniya drones in two hours and ground robots were prime targets. These barriers slowed advances to as little as 200 m in four days but did not stop the operation.

findings.actor: 3rd Army Corps middle-strike drone units
findings.tactic: Starlink-dependent deep drone interdiction
findings.text: Euromaidan Press argued on 22 Oct 2026 that Starlink/Starshield command links and middle-strike drones hitting Russian supply lines were pivotal to Vivaldi, but that a speed cap in force since 14 Oct cuts terminals on drones flying faster than about 160 km/h. A commentator citing Russian sources says Ukrainian deep strikes have fallen significantly; no Russian ground regained has been documented, so the method is degraded rather than defeated (single source).

findings.actor: Russian 25th Combined Arms Army
findings.tactic: Assaults east of Lyman near Zarichne
findings.text: ISW reported that Russian forces concentrated attacks east of Lyman near Zarichne on 20 and 21 Oct 2026 but did not advance. ISW's 18 Oct report likewise showed a geolocated Russian infiltration on Lyman's eastern outskirts without any confirmed advance, and ISW now states that Vivaldi defeated the northern pincer of the planned encirclement.

findings.actor: 1030th Air Defence Regiment 'Aquila' interceptor battalion (3rd Army Corps)
findings.tactic: Interceptor drones against jet-powered Shaheds
findings.text: Euromaidan Press, citing ArmyInform on 21 Oct 2026, reported the battalion's claim to have destroyed several thousand Russian aerial targets during Vivaldi, including Zala, Orlan and Supercam reconnaissance drones. Against jet-powered Shaheds, however, interceptors scored only small numbers because they need 500-600 km/h, and the regiment still relies mainly on guns and SAMs for them.

findings.actor: Ukrainian forces north and east of Lyman
findings.tactic: Pushing to the Zherebets River line
findings.text: ISW's 19 Oct 2026 assessment cited observer Kostyantyn Mashovets that Ukrainian forces had likely pushed Russian troops out of Myrne, reached the Zherebets south of Torske and Myrne and advanced into northern Zarichne, while Russian milbloggers claimed to have lost and retaken positions in southern Zarichne. These gains are not geolocated, and some Russian assault groups still hold positions in the Stavky-Kolodyazi-Myrne-Zarichne area.

findings.actor: Russian 144th Motorized Rifle Division (20th Combined Arms Army)
findings.tactic: Holding the Chornyi Zherebets bridgehead
findings.text: Biletskyi said on 19 Oct 2026 that the 144th Division, which formed much of the grouping on the Chornyi Zherebets bridgehead, had in effect ceased to exist as an organised force, the bridgehead was eliminated and Russia had temporarily dropped its plan to reach Barvinkove via Sviatohirsk. The degradation is a Ukrainian claim, but ISW on 20 Oct judged Russia would have to reconstitute the division before any new Lyman offensive.

assessment.text: Vivaldi's gains held through 23-28 Oct 2026, and Russia's attempts to reverse them failed on the ground. ISW recorded Russian assaults northeast and southeast of Lyman on 22-26 Oct with no advance, and an infiltration north of Lyman ended with the infiltrator struck east of Zelena Dolyna (28 Oct). Ukrainian small-team and robot tactics kept working: NC13 used ground robots and FPVs to stop an assault through a pipe (26 Oct, single source), extending the 22 Oct field accounts of blockade raids. Russia's adaptation is to swap infantry pressure for drones; ISW on 26 Oct corroborated the Varyag brigade's move to Lyman after Rubikon's withdrawal, superseding one drone formation with another, though without regaining ground. Ukraine's next step is contested: mappers claimed crossings of the Zherebets at Makiivka, Novosadove and Terny on 26 Oct, but none is confirmed and AMK reports many repelled assaults. The Starlink speed cap and jet-powered Shaheds remain unsolved constraints, and ISW says Moscow has not dropped its Fortress Belt plan.

timeline.text: The UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2803, endorsing the US Gaza plan, welcoming the Board of Peace and authorising an International Stabilization Force for Gaza.
Israel's security cabinet approved entry of an initial International Stabilization Force of about 200 personnel from countries such as Uganda and Morocco, operating in coordination with the IDF.

The Gaza Division commander said Israel controls 63% of Gaza with almost 40 new outposts, and the IDF published a list of 170 Palestinians reported as slain journalists whom it says belonged to armed groups.

On the first anniversary of the ceasefire Israeli attacks killed at least eight people across Gaza, including an eight-year-old girl, while no stabilisation force had deployed and the Palestinian technocratic committee was still kept out of the Strip.
Israel said private-sector goods would gradually resume entering Gaza after a week-long halt, blamed on Hamas levies on merchants, that had cut daily truck entries from about 600 to about 300.

Israeli media reported a military intelligence assessment that Hamas can only be disarmed through renewed fighting, as a Hamas warning of new attacks inside Israel, the West Bank and abroad was relayed to Israel through the UN humanitarian coordinator.
Israel's Knesset election left Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and Eisenkot's at 48 with Arab parties at a record 19, so no bloc could form a majority and the outgoing government stays on as caretaker.
An Israeli strike on a post in al-Mawasi, Rafah, that screens commercial trucks entering from Kerem Shalom killed four Gaza government employees and wounded about 30.

timeline.text: After Iranian strikes on vessels collapsed the June ceasefire, US Central Command resumed its naval blockade of Iranian ports and struck Iranian anti-shipping targets near Hormuz.

After US strikes on Iranian coastal radars killed 11 people and the IRGC fired anti-ship ballistic missiles at a US carrier and destroyer, CENTCOM destroyed or disabled three Iranian tankers, the Downy, Stark 1 and Kylo.

Trump publicly rejected Iran's seven-day plan after the Wall Street Journal reported he expects to resume bombing after the November midterms, and the next day the IRGC claimed a second US underwater drone captured in the strait, which CENTCOM called 'clearly desperate'.

Trump pledged no attack on Iran before the 3 November midterms while keeping the blockade, after reports that the Pentagon was preparing options to resume major combat, and a tanker caught fire off Fujairah.

The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank after a projectile hit in the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, one of two ships lost within a day, as security data showed at least ten vessels attacked since 11 October.

The IRGC claimed seven tankers hit overnight in and near the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump called fake and no maritime agency confirmed, a day after the New York Times reported US and Israeli plans for a short, intensive strike campaign on Iran after the 3 November midterms.

Qatari mediators delivered a new draft deal and a letter from Vice President Vance to Iran's security chief Rezaei proposing a near-term meeting, as the CENTCOM commander declared the primary Hormuz routes free of mines.

Trump reportedly told Gulf allies to prepare for a brief, intense campaign on Iran after the US midterms, as the IRGC claimed three tankers hit mines on the southern route and UKMTO confirmed one tanker struck by a projectile.

text: Long-range strike versus integrated air and missile defence (Established · Contested) is borne out as latent but imminent: Critical Threats recorded no US or partner strike on Iran in its 23, 25, 26 and 28 Oct updates, yet reporting on 29 Oct said Trump told Gulf allies to prepare for a brief, high-intensity campaign after 3 Nov, and Iran has named Gulf oil sites, cables and data centres as retaliation targets. The defensive question has shifted from Iranian air defence to whether Gulf defences can absorb retaliation. Maritime chokepoint disruption versus energy-route resilience (Established · Contested) is borne out and adapting: Iran now enforces a northern-route rule, claiming mine hits on tankers using the US-promoted southern route on 23 and 29 Oct, while CENTCOM said on 25 and 28 Oct that primary lanes are mine-free; UKMTO confirmed only one projectile hit, on 29 Oct.

Deterrence versus proxy and deniable escalation (Rising · Contested) is borne out: disputed attribution of mine versus projectile hits remains Iran's main lever, and Critical Threats reported on 26 Oct that Iran told Hezbollah it need not join a renewed war, keeping the proxy layer in reserve. Vance's 25 Oct letter shows coercion and diplomacy running in parallel, and adaptability stays High on all three topics.

timeline.text: Thailand and Cambodia signed a ceasefire taking effect at noon, ending 20 days of fighting that killed over 100 people and displaced more than half a million.
Thailand's armed forces chief announced completion of the first 1.3 km of a permanent concrete border wall in Chanthaburi's Pong Nam Ron district, with over 7 km more planned.

The first UNCLOS conciliation session in Singapore (14–16 September) closed with Cambodia tabling three settlement options and Thailand insisting a maritime boundary be delimited before any resource sharing; a second meeting was set for The Hague on 14–18 October.

Prak Sokhonn told the UN General Assembly that the conflict had seriously eroded trust, that over 20,000 Cambodians still cannot return home, that Thailand should implement the December agreements and resume Joint Boundary Commission demarcation, and that the Charter sets no separate standard for powerful states.

Hun Manet said the United States had asked Thailand to stop escalatory actions and encroachment on Cambodian territory, and Thailand's foreign ministry denied it the same day, conditioning any boundary commission meeting on a border secure from landmines and transnational crime.

The second UNCLOS conciliation meeting opened at the Peace Palace in The Hague as Cambodia and Thailand clashed at the UNHCR Executive Committee in Geneva over the more than 20,000 Cambodians Phnom Penh says cannot return home.

The Hague conciliation round closed with the first agreed confidence-building measures (a direct channel between the two navies among them, by Thailand's account), while the Commission noted earlier measures were unimplemented and set a third meeting in Kuala Lumpur for 24–27 November.

Cambodia's culture ministry demanded the return of artefacts Thailand removed from K'nar temple and called Thai activity at disputed border temples a fait accompli, as the Thai army rejected Cambodian charges that its barbed-wire barriers were redrawing the boundary by force.

text: On border incident management versus escalation prevention, the Declining / cautiously improving status is borne out on fire but not on friction: no shooting, drone crossing or mine casualty was reported from 16 to 29 Oct, yet the contest has moved onto heritage ground, with Thailand's culture minister on 25 Oct claiming Ta Kwai and Khana and refusing to return artefacts, and Cambodia on 27 Oct calling this a fait accompli. Incidents are now generated by statements and survey work rather than patrols, which keeps lessons on restraint transferable but narrow. On ceasefire monitoring versus local force autonomy, the trigger has not fired, but local consolidation continues: the Thai army on 27 Oct defended barbed-wire barriers inside what it calls Thai territory, and the informal border-committee meeting on 28 Oct produced no reported agreement, so monitors observe works they cannot reverse.

On regional mediation versus bilateral military signalling, the Background monitor status holds: ASEAN defence ministers endorsed the observer team on 28 Oct and the EU funded joint mine action on 27 Oct, while the Hague measures of 18 Oct have not stopped the public exchanges. Adaptability stays Low.

text: On counter-criminal operations versus sovereignty and escalation, the trigger is still not met: the 27 Oct strike that killed five hit a go-fast vessel in the Eastern Pacific, not national territory, and the legal track lost its presiding judge on 28 Oct, which former prosecutors expect to cost little time. Legitimacy is now contested between a mobilised opposition inside the country and a US-backed interim government. Adaptability stays Medium: the transferable lesson lies in sequencing lawfare, sanctions relief and street pressure, not in new military methods.

timeline.text: Three PLAN warships, including two Type 022 missile boats, and five China Coast Guard cutters intercepted the MV Lapu-Lapu resupply run about 60 nautical miles from Second Thomas Shoal, a warship radioed that it would take 'compulsory measures' and the mission was suspended, the first blocked run since the July 2024 understanding.

A China Coast Guard cutter trained its water cannon on BRP Cabra during a medical evacuation from BRP Sierra Madre, forcing a small-boat transfer four nautical miles off the reef that delayed the mission by nearly ten hours, while a PLA Navy frigate stood nearby.

Chinese maritime militia vessel 9622 deployed 22 sampans around Philippine-held Kota Island, one within about 250 metres of the shore, and its master encircled the Philippine response boats and claimed the area as Chinese before all the vessels left.

The Philippine foreign ministry summoned Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan over his 15 October remark that China 'may easily win' if it used force, calling it provocative and unacceptable, as senators filed a resolution to expel him.

The armed forces completed a rotation-and-resupply run to BRP Sierra Madre without incident, the first since the 24 September interception, while China's coast guard said it had approved and monitored the delivery and Manila denied seeking any permission; the same day PLA Navy ships shadowed USS Charleston near Sabina Shoal.

The carrier Liaoning and three destroyers sailed through the Sulu Sea and the Basilan Strait inside the Philippine archipelago, shadowed by Philippine warships, before heading east toward the Philippine Sea, as Chinese navy ships near Philippine-held features rose to 26 in the week to 26 October.
China sent only its Manila defence attaché to the ASEAN defence ministers' meeting with partners in Cebu, its lowest-level attendance since 2010, blaming obstacles created by the Philippine chair.

text: On grey-zone maritime coercion versus presence and resilience, the Established · Contested status holds, but the coercive weight has shifted toward the navy: after the unhindered 20 Oct resupply, the AFP's 27 Oct count showed 7 PLAN ships alongside 7 coast guard ships at Ayungin, and a Chinese-language paper reported on 23 Oct that Beijing is weighing towing the Sierra Madre (single source). items.whyNow: The battle for Sittwe has turned against the navy, with the Arakan Army reportedly sinking two vessels on 26 Oct, while fighting on the Karen front spilled into Thailand on 29 Oct and the ASEAN Chair's envoy began a humanitarian mission in Myanmar on 28 Oct, so the week shows military pressure on the regime rising at the same moment regional and US engagement with it deepens.
changes: 29 Oct: A shell from a regime assault on KNLA-held Min Let Pan, opposite Mae Sot, wounded a Thai woman in Mahawan subdistrict and damaged more than 20 houses; Thai troops fired warning rounds into Myanmar and reinforced the Moei river line, two days after some 200 Mae Sot residents demanded protection (DVB; Thai Examiner).

29 Oct: DVB reported the Arakan Army accusing the military of using Sittwe residents as human shields by ordering them to demolish bomb shelters, a directive residents confirmed, and said an explosion on Min Bar Gyi Road in central Sittwe on 23 Oct killed at least nine people, with no side claiming it (DVB).

28 Oct: The ASEAN Chair's special envoy, Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro, began a 28–30 Oct humanitarian mission, observing aid distribution in Taunggyi, Shan State, before arriving in Naypyitaw, ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit (Bernama via The Star).

27 Oct: UN Special Rapporteur Kelley Currie told the UN General Assembly Third Committee that Min Aung Hlaing's regime is the greatest source of civilian death in Myanmar and warned that diplomatic engagement legitimises it, as DW reported two rounds of US talks with the military straining the EU's non-recognition policy (DVB; DW via Dhaka Tribune, search summary only).

26 Oct: The Arakan Army reportedly struck three navy vessels, including a frigate, near the Kaladan river mouth off Sittwe, sinking two and damaging one; the AA says it still holds Ngapyi Island and has disabled six vessels in a month (DMG/BNI and DVB, anonymous and AA sources, unverified; Irrawaddy, search summary only).

24 Oct: DMG reported a junta column of about 500 heading from Saw Township toward Kyindwe in southern Chin cut to some 300 by ambushes near Maw Creek, part of a push the Chin People's Army puts at nearly 3,000 troops; Myanmar Now reported on 27 Oct that Chin forces are holding and captured defected BNRA fighters (DMG via BNI, resistance claims; Myanmar Now).

timeline.text: Min Aung Hlaing is inaugurated as president of Myanmar's quasi-civilian military government in Naypyitaw, and on 21 April offers armed groups peace talks with a 100-day deadline that the KNU, CNF and NUG reject.
The military launches 'Operation 4926', a combined land, naval and air offensive against the Arakan Army across Sittwe, Ponnagyun, Kyaukphyu and Gwa townships in Rakhine State.
Six fibre-optic FPV drones strike Tada-U airbase near Mandalay; resistance says Yak-130 jets were hit, the junta says all were intercepted, and international flights are cancelled.

Three junta jets bomb the National Unity Government's regional command near Kyaikto, killing at least six including Air Force defector Nay Win Aung, as the Arakan Army repels a two-week junta attempt on the Maei pass at Mindon, Malaysia sets 29 Sep to begin deporting Myanmar migrants, Myanmar recalls its ambassador to Thailand, a Delhi court lets the foreign drone trainers leave India and an MNDAA delegation opens Chinese-pressed talks in Naypyidaw.

A junta fighter jet drops two bombs on the main wholesale market and adjacent bridge in Kyauktaw, Rakhine State, at about noon, killing at least 33 people and wounding 36 by the Arakan Army's and a senior rescue official's count, the deadliest strike in Rakhine since the December 2025 hospital bombing, with no comment from the military.

Junta warships, artillery and aircraft begin a week of failed landing attempts on Ngapyi Island opposite the Shwe Min Gan naval base near Sittwe, and by 14 October the Arakan Army still holds the island and has taken outposts on the city's edge, by local accounts.

The Arakan Army takes two outposts near Kyarmathauk, about four miles north of the junta's Regional Operations Command in Sittwe, and fights for an engineering battalion there as the air force strikes its positions, by an AA source.

The Arakan Army reportedly struck three navy vessels, including a frigate, near the Kaladan river mouth by the Shwe Min Gan naval base off Sittwe, sinking two, by anonymous military and AA-side accounts.

text: On distributed resistance versus state airpower, the Established · Contested status is borne out: regime aircraft, artillery and drones kept killing civilians, eight in Kyaikto in a week by a KNU count reported on 27 Oct, yet airpower has not reversed ground trends, with the Arakan Army still holding Ngapyi Island and a junta column toward Kyindwe reportedly cut from about 500 to 300 by 24 Oct (resistance estimates). Tactical gains are not yet durable governance: Sittwe remains besieged rather than taken. On commercial UAS and improvised systems versus conventional advantage, the Rising status is reinforced from an unexpected direction: the reported sinking of two navy vessels on 26 Oct (unverified, method unstated) and the regime's order, confirmed by residents on 29 Oct, that Sittwe households demolish shelters to deter artillery and drone strikes show cheap fires shaping a garrison's behaviour.

On fragmented governance versus logistics and civilian resilience, the Established status holds: fighting at Min Let Pan sent fire into Thailand on 29 Oct, while the ASEAN envoy's 28 Oct aid mission and US talks show outsiders dealing with Naypyitaw over access and corridors. Adaptability stays High.

items.whyNow: Daily Houthi salvos now reach the Eastern Province's oil heartland and Riyadh, and the coalition's 26 Oct strikes on launchers and missile tunnels show both sides settling into a sustained missile war, while Egypt's 26 Oct authorisation and the AP-reported Russian satellite link widen the circle of actors. changes: 29 Oct: The coalition said it downed two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, where explosions were heard, and Houthi media said a Saudi strike killed 12 people in Taiz province (Houthi claim, unverified) (CBS live, The National).

28 Oct: After an evacuation warning alleging a Saudi military cargo plane was present, Houthi ballistic missiles hit Aden airport and the adjacent al-Nasr camp, the latest of repeated attacks since mid-October; Houthi media said Saudi strikes killed 14 in Jawf, and government-aligned forces repelled Houthi attacks south of Taiz (Anadolu, CBS live, Critical Threats).

27 Oct: The coalition intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province and four drones over the south, with alerts in the Eastern Province and al-Kharj; an AP report on a private firm's analysis said Russian reconnaissance satellites were over the targets of all 40 Houthi and Iraqi militia strikes on Saudi Arabia from 1 Jul to 19 Oct (Al Jazeera, Al-Monitor).

26 Oct: The coalition said it destroyed four ballistic missile launchers, five storage tunnels and a missile depot around Sanaa after intercepting a Houthi missile at Riyadh airport; Egypt's parliament authorised military help to defend the kingdom, and Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials met Iranian officials in Tehran and agreed to keep talking (Al Jazeera, Critical Threats).

25 Oct: Saudi defences intercepted 11 missiles over the south, with debris injuring two in Asir, after at least 12 missiles and two drones were launched over 24–25 Oct; Riyadh airport reopened, and Gulf sources said Riyadh offered about $1bn via Iran for a ceasefire (single source) (Critical Threats, Al Jazeera).
24 Oct: An air strike reportedly by Saudi Arabia hit Sanaa's Asr district, and Saudi forces intercepted two drones and a missile over Riyadh Province (Al Jazeera, Critical Threats).

timeline.text: The Houthis declare a naval and air blockade of Saudi Arabia in response to a strike on Sanaa airport, ending four years of relative calm under the 2022 truce.

A Houthi missile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid airport, killing 12 people and wounding 309 by Saudi count, the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade, and the airport was shut.
Three Houthi ballistic missiles hit the al-Alam training camp for new security recruits in Shabwa, killing at least 53 people by the local authority's count.
A Houthi attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport killed two people and drone debris at the Shaybah oilfield killed two more, as the US ordered non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed four ballistic missile launchers, five missile storage tunnels and a depot around Sanaa, and Egypt's parliament authorised its military to help defend the kingdom.
Houthi ballistic missiles hit Aden airport and an adjacent security camp after an evacuation warning, damaging the runway in one of repeated attacks on the airport since mid-October.

text: Long-range attack versus layered protection (Rising · Contested) is borne out at higher volume: the Houthis fired at least 12 missiles and two drones over 24–25 Oct, Saudi forces intercepted 11 over the south with debris injuring two in Asir, and three more missiles were aimed at the Eastern Province on 27 Oct. Interception is holding over Saudi cities, but less-defended Aden airport was hit on 28 Oct. The defender is now adapting offensively, striking launchers, storage tunnels and a depot around Sanaa on 26 Oct, while a private analysis reported by AP on 27 Oct linking Russian satellite passes to 40 strikes (single source) suggests the attacker's targeting is externally enabled. Maritime disruption versus route resilience (Established · Contested) is not borne out at sea for now: no Houthi attack on merchant shipping was reported in the fortnight, and the contest stays on land south of Taiz, where Critical Threats recorded Houthi attacks repelled on 25 and 28 Oct.

Regional basing versus militia targeting (Established · Contested) is borne out through widening host-nation commitments rather than attacks on bases: Egypt's parliament authorised defensive aid on 26 Oct, and Critical Threats assessed on 23 Oct that Iraq-based groups very likely launched at least four drones at Saudi Arabia in 20 days. Adaptability is High on the first topic and Medium on the other two.
